title: herbctl
description: the herbstluftwm keybind imperatives: every composite mod- binding as a plain-named verb - the float-register state machines, the navigation chains, the layout cyclers - compiled to a standalone bunli binary.

content.heading: herbctl - the keybind imperatives, as a native binary
content: **herbctl** owns what the keybinds of **herbstluftwm** express as spawn chains: one verb per mod-binding, each issuing the exact hlwm chains the binding expresses, token for token - compiled to a standalone binary with bunli, so the keybinds spawn binaries, not scripts.
the verbs are named by what they do: split-right-cycle, shift-up, minimize-toggle.

content.heading: the chains a keybind spawns
content: an hlwm keybind is a spawn command: the compositor runs one shell line on every key press. the dots bindings chain several herbstclient calls into that line - focus moves, frame splits, layout rotations - held under the hlwm lock so no other client interleaves.

the composite bindings (the float registers especially) outgrew the one-line form: whole state machines, branched on the frame tree, the floating layer and the layout algorithm. that is what herbctl compiles - the autostart spawns ~/.local/bin/herbctl <verb>, and the dots keybind stays a one-word spawn.

content.heading: the package, architecturally
content: one **bunli** binary; the verb surface is declared by the registry below and rendered live - the page never hand-lists verbs, so it stays accurate regardless of the api.
it imports **herbstutil** for its pure primitives only - parseAttr, the typed attribute reader. the composite keybind commands live here, and herbstutil ships none of them.

every spawn (herbstclient and the dots helper binaries) carries the 5-second timeout inherited from herbstutil's spawn layer: a vanished window resolves null instead of wedging the bar or the keybind. every verb is verified against the recorded argv of a mocked herbstclient binary (plus mocked helper binaries) - nothing here needs a live WM to test.

content.heading: usage - the verbs
content: the dots keybinds spawn the compiled standalone binary at ~/.local/bin/herbctl; **on-deploy**'s toolchain step builds and installs it on deploy. each verb gets its own section below.
